newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - July 1.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - July 1.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - Leo Burnett wins 45-million-pound global account for Tambrands' Tampax brand, owned by Procter & Gamble. Leo Burnett won out over FCB. As a result of the account win, the Frankfurt agency Michael Conrad & Leo Burnett will take charge of the brand in Germany and the Roedelheim agency will have to give up a different P&G account. The Tempo brand will move to DMB&B in Frankfurt. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Katjes Fassin GmbH & Co, a sweets manufacturer, awards the advertising account for its Dr. Hillers candy to Agentur Publicis in Frankfurt. Publicis says it won the seven-figure account against rivals Scholz & Friends from Berlin and Boros of Wuppertal. Katjes Fassin plans to launch a new advertising offensive for its peppermint candy brands. (Reuter).
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - ARD, the German public broadcaster, buys the rights to rebroadcast Bundesliga soccer from ISPR GmbH, a sports marketing agency. The deal covers the 1997-1998 soccer season. SAT1, the private German TV network, holds the initial broadcast rights until the year 2000. (Reuter)

BUDAPEST - The privatisation of Hungarian TV is moving forward after seven years of disputes. A consortium called Magyar RTL, which is led by CLF-Ufa, and MTM-SBS, a Swedish-Hungarian consortium, have received two 10-year licenses for private programming, according to ORTT, a Hungarian radio and TV agency. The bid by Central European Media Enterprises (CME), the U.S. media group, fell short of the mark. Herbert Kloiber, the Munich TV mogul, has a stake in MTS-SBS. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Kinderkanal, a German public network for children, is supposed to be included in the cable network in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany's most populous state, within the next several months. Kabel 1, the private network, will be able to hold onto its slot for the time being, the state media agency LfR said. Kinderkanal will be introduced as soon as Deutsche Telekom makes two additional cable stations available. The public network's Phoenix channel will not be included in the state's cable network until a Duesseldorf court rules on a lawsuit from Kabel 1. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Bayerischer Rundfunk takes 10-percent stake in Bavaria Film studio, buying a stake for about 10 million marks ($5.7 million) that belonged to Deutsche Bank. A number of film hits such as Das Boot and The Neverending Story as well as many popular TV series have been filmed at Bavaria Film studio, which is majority-owned by SR and WDR. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Volkswagen AG is planning to build a small version of the "Lup" car in China, according to a newspaper report. The car would be smaller than the Polo, Volkswagen's smallest car. The head of marketing, Robert Buechelhofer, is quoted as saying VW's sales network in China should be expanded. Asia could become VW's largest market by 2005. (Reuter).

KERPEN - CompuNet Computer AG says operating profits shot up to 43 million marks in the first half of the year, a 44-percent increase over the same period a year earlier. Sales rose to 794 million marks from 670 million. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

MUNICH - Gerrit Huy is the new managing director for the German unit of Compaq Computer Corporation. She follows Kurt Dobitsch, who is leaving for personal reasons. Huy, 43, was previsouly a member of the managing board at Debis. (Reuter)
MUNICH - Peter Littmann is the new supervisory board chief of Mondi, a woman's clothing company in Munich and the new chairman of Wuensche AG. (Reuter)
